translation_direction: en → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete English electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Dickens’s comic narrator addresses the reader as bạn throughout; his asides, puns and lists are kept, with partial pun solutions (giống mỡ hơn là giống mộ; kỹ tính quá một ly).
decisions.rationale: The narrator’s voice is half the book’s charm.

decisions.decision: The carol lyric missing from the witness after “at the first sound of” is not supplied; the sentence breaks off as in the source.
Shillings, pence, half-crowns and farthings kept as si-linh, xu, đồng nửa crown, đồng trinh.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: Reader address unified to bạn across the four drafting parts (was quý vị in Stave One).
The long anaphoric ‘not a… but fell upon the heart’ sentence disentangled; 251 calque ‘the veriest old well’ recast.
The narrator’s echo of Scrooge’s ‘Out upon merry Christmas!’ restored (Dẹp cái Giáng sinh vui vẻ đi!); 34 ‘that extremity’ made readable as hell.
The Genii of the Bedreddin Hassan tale no longer misattributed to Aladdin; Treadmill and half-a-crown terms corrected; young Scrooge and Fan pronouns fixed (249–250, 288).
Cross-part consistency: the children call Bob bố, Mrs Cratchit bà, Old Joe lão; spaced dashes in Stave Four; công kênh, lần bước, nguôi ngoai and Scrooge’s ‘Nó biết ta mà’ corrected.
The alphabet love-game is now recognisably a parlour game.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.source_term: Ghost / Spirit; Ghost of Christmas Past, Present, Yet to Come
glossary.draft_rendering: Hồn ma; Hồn ma Giáng sinh Quá khứ, Hiện tại, Tương lai
glossary.rationale: One term for ghost and spirit across all five staves; the three titles are fixed.
Scrooge’s catchword, unchanged wherever it recurs.
Stave headings KHÚC MỘT–NĂM keep the carol conceit of the title.
Fred is the son of Scrooge’s sister Fan; cậu/cháu is the correct Vietnamese kin term.

witness_decision: Selected the complete text of Project Gutenberg #46, which reproduces the first edition (London: Chapman & Hall, December 1843) with John Leech’s illustrations; the illustrations are not reused. Stave headings are kept as text units.

unresolved_questions.explanation: The Spirits/Total Abstinence pun of the last paragraph is not reproduced.
One stacked object in the description of Old Joe’s quarter remains slightly awkward.

title_review.rationale: Bài ca Giáng sinh is the established Vietnamese title; carol is a Christmas song, and the stave headings (Khúc) keep Dickens’s musical conceit.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: Opening ‘Marley was dead’ with the door-nail joke kept.
Final blessing keeps Tiny Tim’s capitalised ‘God bless Us, Every One!’
